title: Genetic Mutations and Variations
objectives: Classify types of DNA sequence variations
Distinguish between germline and somatic mutations
Analyze mutation rates in different genomic regions

mutation_types.title: Mutation Classification
mutation_types.content:
• Point mutations: Silent/missense/nonsense (e.g., Sickle cell: Glu6Val)
  • Frameshifts: Indels in non-3n multiples
  • Dynamic mutations: Trinucleotide repeats (Huntington's CAG expansion)

mutation_origins.title: Mutation Sources
mutation_origins.content:
Endogenous
• Replication errors (1 in 109 bp/cell division)
• Oxidative damage (8-oxoG lesions)
Exogenous
• UV radiation (pyrimidine dimers)
• Chemicals (benzopyrene adducts)

clinical_correlation.title: Mutation Disorders
clinical_correlation.content:
CFTR Mutations in Cystic Fibrosis

ΔF508: Protein misfolding (70% alleles)

G542X: Premature stop codon

faqs.title: FAQs
faqs.content:
Why are some mutations dominant-negative?

The mutant protein interferes with normal protein function (e.g., mutant collagen fibers disrupting tissue integrity in Osteogenesis Imperfecta).
